description_en: A stone memorial pillar from the 14th century.The pillar is located on the side of the motorable from Dullu to Rāvatakoṭa, west of the locality of Kālī Bāzār.The eastern side of the pillar contains an inscription in a Nāgarī script, of which 8 lines can be distinguished. The western side contains eroded engraved decorative patterns of spirals. The top part has been cemented.Typologically the pillar is very similar to others from the area that are dated of the first half of the 14th century, such as the pillars of Sātkhambā (DLK0190) or at Nāulegāũ (DLK0251). Such stone pillars were erected throughout the Karnali Basin from the 13th to the 17th century. They are installed to honor the memory of deceased persons, mostly warriors (Andolfatto 2019).
monument_assessment: Restored, Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages), Surface damages
